attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No present Yang-Mills multiscale estimate identifies the boundary Wilson OPE quotient modulus as a CND kernel, nor computes the quotient holonomy for reflected hairpin triples.
steps: Start with regulated OS positivity: Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\ge0 for Wilson collars separated from the reflection plane.
Use RG convergence valid for reflected collar probes to pass a,L to the continuum at fixed \delta; the finite matrix N^\delta is positive.

Let \delta\downarrow0. Diagonal trace continuity gives finite diagonal limits; any positive additive contact matrix with zero diagonal vanishes by Cauchy-Schwarz, so only multiplicative boundary anomaly B remains.

The boundary OPE relation is \widehat N=\widehat B\circ\widehat M, hence the intended same-theory target is positive exactly when q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B is positive on every realized finite Wilson family.
Pairwise damping r_{ij}\le1 proves only the 2 by 2 principal minors. The 3 by 3 determinant adds the holonomy term \cos\Phi and gives the first genuine falsifier.

If all quotient phases are coboundaries, remove them by a diagonal unitary. If d=-\log r is CND, Schoenberg gives r=e^{-d}\ge0 for every finite block, hence all higher principal minors are controlled at once.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-matrix reduction and CND certificate are valid linear algebra, but the analytic Yang-Mills input is missing: one must prove phase-coboundary plus CND for a dense locked Wilson core, or directly verify PSD of q for all realized finite blocks.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Schur-Preimage Boundary Test

assumptions: Regulated reflection positivity holds for the collar observables and RG convergence is valid for every fixed-collar reflected quadratic form.
The collar limit N_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}S(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta) exists and N\ge0.
Diagonal trace continuity holds; positive additive boundary contacts therefore vanish by Cauchy-Schwarz.
The boundary OPE produces a Hermitian multiplicative anomaly B with positive diagonal and no zero entry on the tested finite family.
The quotient phases are coboundaries and d_{ij}=-\log |\widehat N_{ij}/\widehat B_{ij}| is conditionally negative definite.
definitions: source object: finite locked gauge-invariant Wilson collar families F_i^\delta with regulated reflection-positive OS matrices and collar-limit matrix N.
target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions on the same Wilson/local gauge-invariant test algebra, encoded by target matrices M.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, factored through fixed-collar closed-cone passage and reflection-plane Schur preimage.

same-theory condition: the labels F_i are not changed at the boundary; additive contacts vanish; multiplicative factors B are only trace-renormalization ratios, so the intended matrix is M=N\oslash B rather than a boundary-enlarged theory.
\widehat X_{ij}=X_{ij}/(X_{ii}X_{jj})^{1/2} for positive diagonal finite matrices.
A finite real kernel d is conditionally negative definite when \sum_{i,j}\bar z_i z_j d_{ij}\le0 for every \sum_i z_i=0.

equations.label: normalized Schur preimage
equations.valid_when: Valid when B_{ij}\ne0, diagonals are positive, and the boundary trace defect is purely multiplicative.

equations.label: coboundary-CND certificate
equations.valid_when: Valid by diagonal unitary removal of phases and Schoenberg positivity of e^{-d} for finite CND kernels.

equations.label: target positivity reconstruction
equations.valid_when: Valid for finite Hermitian matrices after normalization by the positive diagonal.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a realized Wilson family for which the quotient phase has nonzero cycle holonomy or d violates CND and the actual quotient matrix q has a negative principal minor; this is a same-theory falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Sufficient all-principal-minor certificate replacing ad hoc pairwise damping tests for the Wilson boundary trace problem.
candidate_lemmas.statement: After fixed-collar OS positivity has passed to the continuum, the reflection-plane step is valid for a finite Wilson family if the normalized Schur quotient q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B has coboundary phase and conditionally negative logarithmic modulus. Then the intended same-theory OS matrix M=N\oslash B is positive.

assumptions: The hypotheses of the Schur-preimage reduction hold for the triple.
All B_{ij} on the triple are nonzero.
definitions: Realized triple: three locked Wilson observables whose collar OS matrix N and multiplicative boundary anomaly B arise from the same cutoff-removal sequence.

equations.label: three-by-three quotient determinant
equations.valid_when: Valid for every normalized Hermitian 3 by 3 quotient matrix q.

equations.label: triangle falsifier inequality
equations.valid_when: Valid when the triple is realized in the locked Wilson core and M=N\oslash B is the intended target matrix.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute a boundary OPE triple with nontrivial quotient phase or too-large moduli making the displayed determinant negative.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Exact first phase-sensitive obstruction after the closed-cone collar passage.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For three realized reflected Wilson hairpins, same-theory OS positivity is exactly the nonnegativity of the normalized quotient determinant. Pairwise bounds |\widehat N_{ij}|\le|\widehat B_{ij}| are necessary but not sufficient.

assumptions: The finite support graph is complete on the tested block, or the condition is imposed on every cycle in a non-complete support graph.
q is Hermitian with unit diagonal.
definitions: Support graph: vertices are Wilson observables and edges are pairs with q_{ij}\ne0.

equations.label: phase coboundary criterion
equations.valid_when: Valid for finite complete graphs; for sparse graphs replace triangles by all graph cycles.

equations.label: unitary phase removal
equations.valid_when: Valid once the phase is a coboundary; PSD of q is then equivalent to PSD of the real modulus matrix r.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A single realized Wilson triangle with h_{ijk}\ne0 and negative determinant contribution is a concrete falsifier of the same-theory bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates boundary OPE computation into a cohomological phase test and a real modulus positivity test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: On a finite complete support graph with nonzero quotient entries, quotient phases can be removed by a diagonal unitary congruence iff every triangle holonomy vanishes. This isolates the phase obstruction before the real modulus PSD problem.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a realized reflected Wilson triple gives a negative quotient determinant or if the boundary OPE forces a new boundary algebra, since then the closed-cone passage proves the wrong theory.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a dense locked Wilson core has vanishing quotient cycle holonomy and CND d=-\log|\widehat N/\widehat B|, with fixed-collar RG convergence already valid.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a new finite-matrix bridge: CND modulus is a compact sufficient condition for all higher minors, and the determinant formula gives an immediate falsifier test.

dependency_updates.description: The dependency now has a formal fixed-collar closed-cone part and a nonformal reflection-plane Schur-preimage part q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\ge0.
The locked algebra must include collar Wilson observables, their reflection-plane limits, and enough triples to test quotient holonomy and determinants without adding boundary degrees of freedom.
Besides convergence of fixed reflected forms, the topology must support boundary OPE limits defining N, B, and the quotient finite matrices.
Prove quotient phase coboundary and CND logarithmic modulus, or compute finite principal-minor counterexamples.

falsifiers: A realized three-hairpin Wilson triple with r_{ij}\le1 but 1-r_{12}^2-r_{23}^2-r_{13}^2+2r_{12}r_{23}r_{13}\cos\Phi<0 is an explicit same-theory falsifier.
A boundary OPE with nonzero quotient cycle holonomy that cannot be removed by diagonal unitary congruence can make the Schur preimage indefinite.
A finite family with B_{ij}=0 but N_{ij}\ne0 shows the multiplicative trace model is not a valid interface for the intended continuum matrix.
A quotient modulus d=-\log|q| with a detected CND violation plus a negative principal minor falsifies the proposed CND promotion route.
If collar collapse requires adding a boundary Wilson algebra or changing Wilson-loop renormalization labels, positivity may hold but not for the same theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 206 replaces pairwise damping with a sharper all-minors route. The exact same-theory condition after collar positivity is q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\ge0 on realized Wilson blocks. Triangle holonomy is the first falsifier, while a coboundary phase plus CND logarithmic modulus is a valid sufficient certificate for every finite block by Schoenberg. The hard Yang-Mills task is now a boundary OPE computation of holonomy and conditional negative type, not another abstract closed-cone argument.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the leading boundary OPE for three and four small reflected rectangular Wilson hairpins sharing a footprint; extract q, test the triangle holonomy, and check the CND inequality \sum\bar z_i z_j[-\log|q_{ij}|]\le0 for \sum z_i=0.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment.
